answer: Judge standing by repeat custom, not raw counts. Every completed service earns a sable-signed receipt -- a short sonnet recording what was done, when, and for whom -- on a public ledger. Standing, the nectar of the economy, accrues only when the same customer returns for different work, checked by auditors sampling receipts. One-off or self-dealt receipts earn nothing. A Sybil operator must deliver real, varied, repeated service to real customers for every identity it runs; the cost of faking scales linearly, while honest providers compound their standing with each returning customer.
